title: AWS (read-only IAM role: SecurityAudit managed policy)

checks.title: The root user has MFA enabled, or has no credentials
checks.scope: The AWS account's root user only; IAM Identity Center and federated users are not visible here. A root user whose password, access keys and signing certificates were all deleted (centralized root access) passes, as in AWS Security Hub IAM.9 (read 2026-10-26).

checks.title: The root user has no access keys
checks.scope: The AWS account's root user only.

checks.title: Each IAM user with a console password has MFA
checks.scope: IAM users in the account (from the IAM credential report); federated and Identity Center users are not IAM users and are not seen.

checks.title: Each active IAM access key was rotated within 90 days
checks.scope: Long-term access keys of IAM users; roles and temporary credentials have no keys to rotate.

checks.title: The account password policy requires 14 characters and prevents reuse
checks.scope: Console passwords of IAM users in the account.

checks.title: A multi-region CloudTrail trail is logging, with log file validation
checks.scope: Management events in the account; data events and what reads the logs are not checked.

checks.title: Each CloudTrail trail encrypts its log files with a KMS key
checks.scope: Log files the trail delivers to S3; who can read the bucket is not checked.

checks.title: GuardDuty has an enabled detector in the region
checks.scope: Each region given with --aws-regions; which protection plans are on and how findings are handled are not checked.

checks.title: Security Hub CSPM (standards and control checks) is enabled in the region
checks.scope: Each region given with --aws-regions. The result is Security Hub CSPM's (DescribeHub); the detail also says whether the newer AWS Security Hub is on (DescribeSecurityHubV2), which alone does not pass. Enabled standards and the findings themselves are not checked.

checks.title: An AWS Config recorder is recording in the region
checks.scope: Each region given with --aws-regions; which resource types are recorded is not checked.

checks.title: S3 Block Public Access is on at the account level (all four settings)
checks.scope: Every S3 bucket in the account; access points and other services' public endpoints are not covered.

checks.title: Each S3 bucket has default encryption
checks.scope: S3 buckets the account owns. S3 has applied SSE-S3 to every new object since January 2023; the detail names the algorithm.

checks.title: EBS encryption by default is on in the region
checks.scope: New EBS volumes in each region given; volumes created before the setting are not checked.

checks.title: Each RDS DB instance has encrypted storage
checks.scope: RDS and Aurora DB instances in the regions given.

checks.title: Each RDS DB instance is not publicly accessible
checks.scope: RDS and Aurora DB instances in the regions given; security groups in front of them are judged by sg_no_open_admin_ports.

checks.title: Each RDS DB instance keeps automated backups (retention of 1 day or more)
checks.scope: RDS and Aurora DB instances in the regions given; whether the retention meets the recovery objectives is a person's call.

checks.title: No security group allows SSH (22) or RDP (3389) from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
checks.scope: Ingress rules of security groups in the regions given; network ACLs and prefix lists are not evaluated.

checks.title: Each enabled symmetric customer-managed KMS key has automatic rotation on
checks.scope: Customer-managed KMS keys with AWS_KMS key material in the regions given; imported, asymmetric and HMAC keys cannot rotate automatically and are left out.

checks.title: At least one AWS Backup plan exists in the region
checks.scope: Each region given; which resources the plans select and whether restores work are not checked.

checks.title: Each VPC has an active flow log
checks.scope: VPCs in the regions given; subnet- and interface-level flow logs are not counted.

checks.title: IAM Access Analyzer has an active analyzer in the region
checks.scope: Each region given; the analyzer's findings are not read.

checks.title: No IAM user's console password and active access keys have all gone unused for 90 days
checks.scope: IAM users with a console password or an active access key, from the IAM credential report (password_last_used, access_key_N_last_used_date); a credential never used counts from its creation (IAM User Guide, credential reports, read 2026-10-26). --aws-inactive-days changes the limit. Federated and Identity Center users are not IAM users and are not seen. Prowler's iam_user_console_access_unused and iam_user_accesskey_unused cover the same ground for a client that runs Prowler; this one serves a role kept at SecurityAudit alone.

checks.title: No S3 bucket is public through its bucket policy or its ACL
checks.scope: Each bucket the account lists. Passes at once when the account's and the bucket's Block Public Access settings together set RestrictPublicBuckets and IgnorePublicAcls; otherwise GetBucketPolicyStatus (IsPublic) and GetBucketAcl (effective grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers) decide (Amazon S3 User Guide, Block Public Access, read 2026-10-26). Object ACLs and access points are not read. Prowler's s3_bucket_public_access is the same idea; this one serves a role kept at SecurityAudit alone.

checks.title: GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 is on in the region
checks.scope: Each region given: an ENABLED detector whose EBS_MALWARE_PROTECTION feature is ENABLED (GetDetector features, or the older dataSources.malwareProtection; GuardDuty API Reference, read 2026-10-26). It scans the EBS volumes of instances GuardDuty finds suspicious; Malware Protection for S3, agents on the instances and the scan results are not read. Prowler has no check for it.

checks.title: Each running EC2 instance is COMPLIANT in Systems Manager Patch Manager
checks.scope: Running EC2 instances in each region given (DescribeInstances), against ListResourceComplianceSummaries with ComplianceType Patch (AWS Systems Manager API Reference, read 2026-10-26). An instance with no Patch summary fails: it is not a managed node or Patch Manager never scanned it. The patch baseline decides what COMPLIANT means; it is not read. On-premises managed nodes, containers and Lambda are not judged. Prowler's ssm_managed_compliant_patching covers managed instances for a client that runs Prowler; this one also fails a running instance Systems Manager does not know, and serves a role kept at SecurityAudit alone.
